description: Somos Kiki y Carlo Catalini, estudiantes de nivel secundario y formamos parte del Club STEAM VCP. Nos apasionan la tecnología, la ciencia y la innovación, y buscamos desarrollar soluciones creativas que generen un impacto positivo en la sociedad y el ambiente.
summary:
FireWatch is an interactive platform designed to improve the analysis and monitoring of wildfires using NASA FIRMS. Inspired by the devastating wildfires in Córdoba, Argentina, we aim to address a key challenge in satellite-based fire monitoring: differences in spatial resolution and detection capabilities can create misleading trends, making it difficult to distinguish real changes in fire activity from differences between sensors.

Our solution allows users to select any geographic area on an interactive map, retrieve current and historical fire detections, and compare satellite datasets over the same period. By harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS observations onto a common 1 km grid, FireWatch enables more consistent comparisons, identifies anomalies in fire activity, and evaluates detection patterns through statistical validation.

This project is important because reliable environmental data is essential for understanding wildfire dynamics, identifying unusual activity, and supporting better-informed prevention and emergency response decisions. FireWatch transforms complex satellite observations into accessible, meaningful information that can help protect ecosystems and vulnerable communities.
details:
FireWatch is a web-based platform developed by CataTech to improve wildfire monitoring and historical fire analysis through NASA satellite data. Every year, wildfires devastate thousands of hectares in Córdoba, Argentina, threatening native forests, biodiversity, and local communities. FireWatch addresses a critical challenge: comparing fire activity across satellites with different spatial resolutions without producing misleading conclusions.

The platform integrates MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) active fire detections into a unified analytical framework. Its five main solutions are:

  • Interactive geographic analysis: Users draw polygons on a map to select and analyze any region of interest.
  • Automated data integration: The platform retrieves NASA FIRMS data and combines satellite records in one interface.
  • Spatial harmonization: Both sensors are projected onto a common 1 km grid, allowing fire activity to be measured by active cell-days rather than incompatible detection counts.
  • Cross-satellite comparison: A color-coded visualization identifies coincident and individual satellite detections, with 3 km aggregation and adjustable mathematical controls.
  • Historical Calendar: Users compare monthly fire activity against previous-year medians while distinguishing days without detected fires from days with unavailable data.

FireWatch transforms complex satellite datasets into accessible, actionable information. Its intended impact is to help researchers, environmental organizations, and emergency-management teams identify genuine changes in fire activity, understand historical patterns, and make better-informed prevention decisions.

The project combines JavaScript, web technologies, NASA FIRMS data services, and a serverless backend hosted on Vercel. Its creative contribution is not simply visualizing satellite detections, but addressing the inconsistencies between different satellite generations through a transparent, reproducible harmonization methodology.

Full documentation on GitHub: https://github.com/kiki2010/FireWatch

By making satellite-based fire analysis interactive and accessible, FireWatch aims to support more informed decisions and contribute to the protection of Córdoba's native forests and communities.
